test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is not a 'Ghana Vadya'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mridangam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ghana Vadya** refers to the category of Indian classical musical instruments that produce sound primarily through solid vibrating materials without the need for strings or membranes.
 
• Examples of Ghana Vadya include instruments like **Manjira, Jaltarang, and Khartal**, which create sound through striking, shaking, or other solid resonating methods.
 
• **Mridangam**, on the other hand, is a **Avanaddha Vadya** (percussion instrument) that generates sound through the vibration of stretched membranes.
 
• The Mridangam is a barrel-shaped drum used predominantly in Carnatic and other South Indian classical music.
 
• Thus, **Mridangam** does not belong to the Ghana Vadya category, making it the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghana Vadya:**

 
 
• Ghana Vadya instruments are also called solid instruments or idiophones.
 
• These instruments are struck, shaken, or scraped to produce sound.
 
• Common examples include cymbals (Manjira), gongs, bells, and xylophones.
 
 
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya:**
 
 
• Avanaddha Vadya, or percussion instruments, produce sound by vibrating stretched membranes.
 
• Examples include Mridangam, Tabla, Dhol, and Pakhawaj.
 
• These instruments are used in various forms of Indian classical and folk music.
 
 
 
• **Mridangam:**
 
 
• Mridangam is a double-headed drum traditionally made of jackwood and leather.
 
• It is played with hands and is an essential instrument in Carnatic music performances.
 
 
 
• **Jaltarang:**
 
 
• Jaltarang is a unique Ghana Vadya that consists of water-filled porcelain bowls of different sizes.
 
• It produces sound by striking the bowls with sticks.
